reason: A general division ('dividida en 5 sectores primarios', '5 secteurs') of an organ the examples do not name. Like 'segment' in the previous review, it needs the organ it belongs to. When the organ is named, the count can be read as a quality of that organ (pattern 03).

'swelling' was rejected on 2026-11-14 as a general part on different organs (here a corolla or perianth tube, elsewhere other organs). When the organ is named, it is the base region of that organ (FLOPO_0985024 plant organ base) with swollen (PATO_0001851) and its length or diameter, not a new part.

target: labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028) part of epichile (FLOPO_0986029), with position median (FLOPO_0991381); patterns 12 and 18
reason: The middle lobe of the orchid epichile. Both classes exist. 'median lobe' alone was rejected only because it had no organ, and here the organ is named.
Exact: the hyphenated spelling of androgynophore, a class added on 2026-11-13. Fix the hyphen when the word is normalized.

target: leaf lamina (PO_0020039) with surface context abaxial ('lower surface' in flora_context_words.tsv)
reason: 'blade' is a synonym of leaf lamina, and 'lower surface' is already the abaxial surface context. The phrase was not split into the part and its context word.

target: leaf lamina (PO_0020039) with stage context seedling development stage (PO_0007131)
reason: Seedling descriptions (the first leaves after the cotyledons). Leaf lamina plus the seedling stage is right but loses the word 'first'. config/bearer_positions.tsv has no ordinal position for 'first' in a series, and this is too rare to add one.

target: petiole (PO_0020038) with stage context seedling development stage (PO_0007131); pattern 04
reason: The petiole of the seedling's leaves. 'seedling' is already a stage context word, so the phrase should be split into the stage and the petiole.

Narrower: a glandular patch, here kidney-shaped or rhombic glands at the leaf base or between the petioles, as 'gland' was grounded before. Where it is on the petiole or leaf base it is probably an extrafloral nectary (PO_0009057), but the examples do not show nectar, so the broader class is used.

'appendicule' is a small appendage of an organ the examples do not name (it can be absent, fimbriate, retuse or lacerate). 'appendage', 'appendice' and 'appendiculae' were all rejected as general parts that need their organ.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) part of leaf sheath (PO_0020104); pattern 12
reason: The hairs of the leaf sheath. PO has trichome and leaf sheath but no leaf sheath trichome, so it is expressed as a part of a qualified whole.

Narrower: a nectar-secreting outgrowth. The 2026-11-14 review grounded 'fossette nectarifère' to nectary in the same way. Only its shape and how visible it is are described, which a nectary can carry.

A wrong singular of 'soboles' (suckers, shoots from underground parts). PO splits suckers by where they arise: root-borne shoot system (PO_0004544) and shoot-borne shoot system (PO_0004545), and the examples do not say which. Fix the lemma first. If the family shows where the suckers arise, ground them then.
Narrower: the spur of the Melastomataceae connective is one kind of the connective appendage class (an outgrowth of the connective projecting beyond the pollen sacs).

target: leaflet (PO_0020049), counted in collections of size 2, like the 'jugate' rule in flora_counted_parts.tsv; pattern 03
reason: '2 à 4 paires de folioles' is the number of pairs of leaflets, the same reading as '3-jugate'. Add 'pair(s) of leaflets' and 'paires de folioles' as forms of that counted-part rule.

The Latin case form of 'lobus' ('calyx 5 lobis', 'lobis quinque'): a general lobe, which needs its organ. When the organ is named, the lobe class of that organ takes the count (calyx 5 lobis = calyx lobe FLOPO_0986005, count 5). Normalize the Latin form to 'lobe'.

target: extrafloral nectary (PO_0009057) part of leaf rachis (PO_0020055); pattern 12
reason: The glands on the leaf rachis between leaflet pairs (Fabaceae such as Inga and Acacia) are extrafloral nectaries, and PO lists 'petiolar gland' under that class.

'glochidium' and 'glochidia' are already synonyms of trichome in PO, so the grounding failure is a lemma problem ('glochidiae'). The examples are septate and dark brown, which is the Azolla type on massulae. Do not ground to FLOPO glochid (FLOPO_0986043), which is defined as the barbed bristle on cactus areoles.

The arms of a stellate hair ('the rays 6–8', 'straight rays short'). PO has no trichome arm, and multicellular trichome branch cell (PO_0025163) is a cell, not an arm. Two floras are too few for a class. A 'trichome arm' could be a later PO request if it recurs.

target: syconium (FLOPO_0986130): the thickness and shrivelling of its wall as qualities of the syconium
reason: In the Ficus accounts 'receptacle' means the fig. Its wall being shrivelled or 0.5–3 mm thick when dry describes the syconium. Flower receptacle (PO_0009064) is wrong here. If a Dorstenia receptacle is meant, the bearer changes, so confidence is medium.
Exact: PO lists 'spur', 'bud spur' and 'brachyblast' as synonyms of short shoot.
Narrower or exact: the extension of the connective beyond the thecae (capitate, lobed, rugulose) is the outgrowth defined by connective appendage.

Narrower: pellucid or dark gland dots in leaves (Myrtaceae, Rutaceae, Primulaceae) are secretory cavities, and PO lists 'oil cavity' as a synonym of oil gland. The 2026-11-14 review noted that 'translucent' and 'pellucid' describe these dots.

Exact: 'mid-rib' is already a PO synonym of leaf midvein, so this is a hyphen or tokenization miss. When the clause names a bract or sepal instead of a leaf, the midrib belongs to that organ and leaf midvein does not apply.
Exact: the false stem of Musaceae, Zingiberales and similar plants, built from rolled leaf sheaths, is PO pseudostem.

target: perianth lobe (FLOPO_0986004) with region apex (plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023)
reason: A region of an existing class. The length, width, colour and indumentum of the tips are said of the apical region of the perianth lobe.
Sterile bracts on the stem or scape below the inflorescence. flora_context_words.tsv already reads 'stem' as cauline for leaves; extend that rule to 'bract'.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) part of bladder trap (FLOPO_0986084); pattern 12
reason: The glandular and dorsal capillary hairs of the Utricularia trap, counted and described as simple or branched. Bladder trap exists. The large dorsal 'antennae' are not strictly trichomes, so confidence is medium.

Narrower: extra, often minute and subulate bracts, for example calycular bracts below an Asteraceae involucre. They are certainly bracts, but which kind depends on the family, so the general class is used. 'accessory' alone was rejected as an adjective.

Ambiguous: the scales inside the calyx of Gentianaceae and Apocynaceae (squamellae, which are colleters, FLOPO_0986023), or scale-like sepal outgrowths elsewhere (flat, tawny, vesiculose). Without the family this cannot be grounded. 'scale' alone was rejected as a general part.

The examples do not show whether this is the moss spore capsule calyptra (PO_0030037, lobed at the base) or a floral calyptra (calyptra calyx PO_0025329 or calyptra corolla PO_0025330). 'lobe' needs its organ. When the organ is known, the count of lobes and 'incurved' are qualities of that calyptra (pattern 03), and the lobe length is a ratio to the calyptra (pattern 10).
